scope: First public installation and ordinary recovery/compatible updates of this configuration; no old project import, historical services, card registration or migration grants

configuration.current_only: One current normalized HTTPS base URL, device ID, device credential, instance and local-only mode. No retained old service profile or credential lookup by historical instance.
configuration.input: network_sync_configure_service(url,pairing_code,local_only); the R05 page supplies these existing settings. OK acknowledges exact durable settings or an identical no-op, not completion of server pairing.
configuration.url: HTTPS DNS/punycode or IPv4/bracketed IPv6, optional port and path; host/default HTTPS port/trailing slash normalized by the routed implementation. Credentials, query/fragment, ambiguous path separators/dot segments, controls and truncation rejected. Full paths joined without fallback to an author address. Outgoing URI encoding escapes raw UTF-8/unsafe bytes without changing the stored normalized base or double-encoding existing percent escapes; backend decoded routing and public redirects/cookie paths use server-relay/relay/web.py.
configuration.tls: All ESP transports use the pinned certificate bundle, normal peer/hostname validation, clock synchronization and disabled redirects. No self-signed bypass or user trust override. Syntax/host integration is tested in R03; real ESP domain/IP certificate behavior remains R12.
configuration.local_only: Disables credential access and automatic pairing/upload without deleting Wi-Fi or recordings. Retains only the current setting; resuming the same service without a new code preserves its credential or unfinished candidate.
configuration.new_destination: Replaces the current target/candidate only after normal local admission. Never sends the previous token to the new address and never asks the old server for authorization.
configuration.public_view: network_sync_get_service_config returns the redacted memo_config_public_t; token, pairing code and enrollment ID never returned by this getter. configured means enabled and durably finalized device pairing, not provider readiness.

persistence.namespace: memo_cfg1 in the existing default NVS partition
persistence.encoding: Explicit byte serialization, schema/generation, bounded strings, instance bytes and CRC; no native-struct/padding serialization. The routed codec is the only byte-layout definition.
persistence.acknowledgement: Each changed snapshot is written, committed and compared byte-for-byte with readback before success. An identical operation need not rewrite durable state.
persistence.uncertain_io: Write/commit/readback error has unknown old/new durable outcome. No success or credential access until reopening and reloading actual valid durable bytes. Worker/user retry does this automatically when idle; corruption/unknown schema is not treated as a new installation.
persistence.missing: Only a real NOT_FOUND yields the fresh local-only/unpaired default. Ordinary I/O errors never cause erase, fallback to an older credential or overwrite of unknown data.
persistence.updates: Compatible releases preserve this schema and namespace. A future incompatible byte layout needs a new schema and separately scoped conversion; old readers reject it without erase. No import of old-author memo_net/memo_cfg/migration records.

pairing_recovery.intent: Before the first HTTP request, persist one canonical random enrollment UUID, 32 random bytes as lowercase hexadecimal candidate token and the pairing code under the requested normalized URL.
pairing_recovery.creation: POST /v1/enrollments replays the same durable tuple after loss/reboot. Validate returned enrollment ID/device/instance/phase; durably bind observed instance before activation.
pairing_recovery.replay: A bound unfinished candidate first reads anonymous /v1/info and validates its current instance/protocol before sending that candidate again. Each attempt repeats create/activate/finalize idempotently; no separate user continuation operation or per-phase historical journal.
pairing_recovery.completion: Validate matching tuple and finalized phase, then persist paired state. Device credentials remain unavailable until that local commit/readback succeeds. Clear temporary code/transaction fields on success.
pairing_recovery.failure: Transport/lost/invalid response retains the same pending candidate for automatic retry. Explicit invalid/expired/revoked/superseded pairing and confirmed instance replacement return to unpaired under short admission; a normal new pairing code can start again. Never use a mismatching receipt or generate a replacement candidate merely because a response was lost.

operation_admission.short: Atomic AUDIO/COMMIT exclusion covers service and SSID writes; audio startup may wait up to its existing deadline. Emergency audio close can re-enter its single application AUDIO owner. No short COMMIT claim held during HTTP/clock/association wait.
operation_admission.service: Existing HTTP exclusion serializes target/credential changes with requests. Mutations fail busy during recording/playback, SD read/active SD attempt, stream HTTP or unique unconfirmed cardless audio/recovery. No history/card inventory proof.
operation_admission.queues: Changing settings/unknown save results immediately stop unstarted RAM queue intent as in R03. R04 durable per-file task and target rules are defined solely in firmware-tasks-v1.json: a different target cannot resume old intent/state, local-only pauses automatic requests, same service credential refresh uses only the current credential. Old ID-only cursor/manual hints no longer authorize work.
operation_admission.accepted_remote_work: Already durably received SD tasks continue independently on their original server/provider snapshot; ordinary configuration does not migrate them. Current per-record binding/hash/cache behavior and explicit retry are defined by firmware-tasks-v1.json.
operation_admission.wifi: Wi-Fi save changes only the existing wifi namespace/format, checks actual writes/commit/fresh-handle readback, and reports uncertainty rather than success. It uses the same short audio gate but may restore connectivity while stopped cardless audio is retained; it never changes the service identity or drops that audio. Existing multi-key Wi-Fi data is not promised as an atomic whole-list transaction.

portal.session: Temporary WPA2 hotspot; GET /service requires the fixed AP Host and matching Origin if provided, and returns a fresh per-start csrf. Mutating routes require matching Host/Origin, application/json and X-Memo-CSRF. CSRF is internal, not a user input. NUL/depth/body bounds are ordinary JSON transport validation, no history proof.
portal.view: GET /service exposes success, server_url, local_only, configured, pairing, connected, message, csrf. No credential, pairing code, instance UUID, history or media list is displayed.
portal.save: POST /service accepts server_url, pairing_code and local_only. Calls the existing network_sync_configure_service synchronously; success acknowledges durable settings only. Pairing runs automatically on the normal station worker after explicit hotspot close; while the AP is open the view says pending connection rather than claiming a running/completed pairing. Busy/invalid/uncertain writes return success=false and comprehensible error; ordinary retry is available. Polling shows actual current pairing/config state.
portal.wifi: POST /submit accepts ssid and password only; obtains an IP and saves via existing guarded SSID persistence. Wi-Fi connection/failure and service-save/failure are independent; neither silently closes the page or erases recordings. Firmware limits SSID/password byte lengths; hidden SSID and empty password are supported.
portal.exit: POST /exit, with the same session guard, explicitly closes the hotspot. No pairing-completion prerequisite; station worker continues pending pairing automatically.
portal.browser: Only one mutation in flight from the page; buttons recover on failure. Status fetch failure retries and recovers buttons automatically. Empty pairing input retains the current paired/pending same service; no hidden confirmation or migration controls.
